scope: Kubernetes v1.36.1 server-side dry runs of an empty synthetic legacy Secret and an inert Opaque Secret, with a namespace-scoped admission policy. The case also verifies the native tracking ConfigMap and a type-based inventory query. Credential migration and production scope remain separate. A case-owned Pod also makes one actual projected short-lived token read of a named inert ConfigMap over verified API-server HTTPS; the token and response body are never retained. Scratch supplement uses an isolated Kind control-plane profile with only the legacy service-account signer path explicitly empty, while projected TokenRequest credentials remain enabled. It proves deletion of an empty annotated sentinel; Secret data values are never observed.

Admission allows an inert Opaque Secret in a dry run
The type query succeeds and neither dry run persists a Secret
The built-in tracking ConfigMap records a monitoring start date
The disposable controller-manager has the legacy signer path explicitly empty and excludes the legacy token controller
The synthetic token Secret references no existing ServiceAccount
The empty annotated sentinel persists and is inventoried by metadata only
